newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: F.J.Benjamin offers 50 mln shares in Singapore IPO.
newsitem.headline: F.J.Benjamin offers 50 mln shares in Singapore IPO.

text.p: Clothing retailer F.J. Benjamin Holdings Ltd said on Tuesday it was offering 50 million new shares at Singapore $0.80 each in its Singapore initial public offering (IPO).
F.J. Benjamin said in a statement 10 million shares would be placed out and the remainder offered to the public.
The offer would raise net proceeds of about S$37 million which would be used to reduce bank borrowings, for overseas expansion and for working capital.
The shares, to be listed on the mainboard of the Stock Exchange of Singapore (SES), were being offered at a historical price earnings ratio of 11 times, it said.
For the financial year ended June 30, 1996, the company recorded a net profit of S$10.9 million on a turnover of S$255.07 million.
The share offer will close on November 12. The shares will start trading on November 14 on a when-issued basis.
